MRK.rationale: MRK's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings collapse: EPS of -$1.72 versus +$2.01 a year prior, driven by a $9B one-time Cidara charge and a $5.8B Terns acquisition R&D hit, producing a GAAP net loss of -$4.24B. While revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, operating income swung to -$3.53B from +$5.90B. The stock has rallied 66% over the past year to $130.48, pushing the P/E to 36.1x—near the top of its 365-day range (11.1–36.1) and far above the ~12–15x range that prevailed for most of the prior year. P/B has expanded from 4.0x to 7.0x. This extreme valuation expansion has occurred precisely as fundamentals deteriorated: net margin collapsed from ~29.6% to 13.6%, ROE from 36.7% to 19.5%. The forward P/E of 48.3x and PEG of 12.06 signal the market is pricing in aggressive future growth that must be delivered against the looming 2028 Keytruda patent cliff. GARDASIL declined 22% in Q1, and the LITESPARK-012 readout failed. The next earnings event (Aug 4) is a near-term catalyst, but given the stretched valuation and fundamental headwinds, the risk is asymmetrically to the downside. The stock is expensive versus its own history, fundamentals are deteriorating on a GAAP basis, and there is no credible near-term re-rating catalyst to the upside—only a binary earnings event that could disappoint.
